mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized suggests inflationary pressures that may lead the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain positive or neutral in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a tightening labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and pressure corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain positive or neutral in > 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain positive or neutral in > 60% of instances where HOUST decreases by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month indicates a strong supply-side response to demand, which can lead to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain negative or neutral in > 60% of instances where INDPRO increases by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over three consecutive months signals an easing monetary policy, which is generally supportive of equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain negative or neutral in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 7% and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it indicates a potential economic recovery phase, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain negative or neutral in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 7% and FEDFUNDS < 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 5% quarter-over-quarter signals strong consumer demand, which can boost corporate earnings and lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain negative or neutral in > 60% of instances where RSAFS increases by more than 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) growth is negative for two consecutive months and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3%, it suggests a supply-side contraction under tight monetary conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO negative growth for 2 months and FEDFUNDS > 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward returns remain positive or neutral in > 60% of instances where INDPRO shows negative growth for two months and FEDFUNDS > 3%.
